# QA Story 832: Manage clients and properties with access details

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaning business owner, I want to manage clients and their properties — addresses, parking notes, entry method (key/lockbox/alarm codes), pets, and cleaning preferences — so that every job automatically carries authoritative entry and scope information and cleaners never get locked out or blindsided. (Research: key/entry management is a chronic owner burden; scattered access info is a top cleaner pain — docs/research/cleaner-pain-points.md §1.7, §2.2)

## Acceptance criteria

- Add a property under an existing client
- Reject a property with no client
- Save a property with a valid service address
- Reject a property with a blank address
- Job brief inherits property access details
- Updated code propagates to future jobs
- Entry code change is logged
- Deactivate a client with upcoming jobs
- Block hard delete of a client with upcoming jobs

Every finding you uncover during execution gets filed via

`mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__submit_qa_result` with the structured

- **`status: "pass"`** with `issue_ids: []` is fine.
- **`status: "partial"` or `"fail"`** with `issue_ids: []` is **rejected
  by the tool**. A failure with no filed issue is a finding that just
  disappeared when your session ended — there's nowhere else for it to
  live. File the issues first, then submit.
- The bare `submit_qa_result` (without the `mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__`
  prefix) does NOT resolve — use the fully-qualified name.
- Don't write findings into a result.md file. The harness doesn't read it.
  Screenshots and other evidence still belong on disk, but the canonical
  record is the DB attempt + linked issues.

1	# QA Plan — Cleaner CRM
2	
3	## App Overview
4	
5	Cleaner CRM is a Phoenix 1.8 + LiveView 1.2 app backed by Postgres (Ecto), single OTP release with one endpoint. In dev it listens on **http://127.0.0.1:4100** (`PORT` defaults to 4100 in `config/runtime.exs`; port 4000 is occupied by another app on this machine). Authentication is session-based via phx.gen.auth with magic-link *and* password login at `/users/log-in` (POST `/users/log-in` sets the session cookie; protected routes 302-redirect to the login page when unauthenticated). One router (`CleanerCrmWeb.Router`) with a `:browser` pipeline (CSRF-protected, `fetch_current_scope_for_user`) and a currently-unused `:api` pipeline; authenticated LiveViews live under the `:require_authenticated_user` live_session (`/users/settings`, `/accounts*`, `/integrations`), and domain surfaces (clients, schedule, quotes, invoices, field app) will mount under the same session as they are built. Dev extras: `/dev/dashboard` (LiveDashboard) and `/dev/mailbox` (Swoosh local mailbox — where magic-link and invitation emails land).
6	
7	## Tools Registry
8	
9	### Vibium browser (LiveView pages)
10	
11	Use for anything interactive: LiveView forms, navigation, acknowledgment flows, screenshots. Start with `browser_start`, then `browser_navigate` to `http://127.0.0.1:4100`. Probed login form selectors (REAL, from the rendered page): the login page renders two forms — magic-link first, then password. Password login fields: `input[name="user[email]"]`, `input[name="user[password]"]`, checkbox `input[name="user[remember_me]"]`; CSRF is a hidden `_csrf_token` input handled automatically by form submit. Log in by filling the password form and submitting; success redirects to `/`. Example: `browser_navigate {url: "http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in"}` → `browser_fill {selector: "input[name=\"user[email]\"]", value: "qa-owner@cleanercrm.test"}` → fill password → `browser_click` the password form's submit button.
12	
13	### curl (controllers, redirects, response codes)
14	
15	Use for public pages, redirect assertions, and any future JSON/API pipeline. Unauthenticated probe results: `GET /` → 200, `GET /users/log-in` → 200, `GET /users/settings` → 302 (to log-in). # QA Plan — Cleaner CRM

## App Overview

Cleaner CRM is a Phoenix 1.8 + LiveView 1.2 app backed by Postgres (Ecto), single OTP release with one endpoint. In dev it listens on **http://127.0.0.1:4100** (`PORT` defaults to 4100 in `config/runtime.exs`; port 4000 is occupied by another app on this machine). Authentication is session-based via phx.gen.auth with magic-link *and* password login at `/users/log-in` (POST `/users/log-in` sets the session cookie; protected routes 302-redirect to the login page when unauthenticated). One router (`CleanerCrmWeb.Router`) with a `:browser` pipeline (CSRF-protected, `fetch_current_scope_for_user`) and a currently-unused `:api` pipeline; authenticated LiveViews live under the `:require_authenticated_user` live_session (`/users/settings`, `/accounts*`, `/integrations`), and domain surfaces (clients, schedule, quotes, invoices, field app) will mount under the same session as they are built. Dev extras: `/dev/dashboard` (LiveDashboard) and `/dev/mailbox` (Swoosh local mailbox — where magic-link and invitation emails land).

## Tools Registry

### Vibium browser (LiveView pages)

Use for anything interactive: LiveView forms, navigation, acknowledgment flows, screenshots. Start with `browser_start`, then `browser_navigate` to `http://127.0.0.1:4100`. Probed login form selectors (REAL, from the rendered page): the login page renders two forms — magic-link first, then password. Password login fields: `input[name="user[email]"]`, `input[name="user[password]"]`, checkbox `input[name="user[remember_me]"]`; CSRF is a hidden `_csrf_token` input handled automatically by form submit. Log in by filling the password form and submitting; success redirects to `/`. Example: `browser_navigate {url: "http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in"}` → `browser_fill {selector: "input[name=\"user[email]\"]", value: "qa-owner@cleanercrm.test"}` → fill password → `browser_click` the password form's submit button.

### curl (controllers, redirects, response codes)

Use for public pages, redirect assertions, and any future JSON/API pipeline. Unauthenticated probe results: `GET /` → 200, `GET /users/log-in` → 200, `GET /users/settings` → 302 (to log-in). Session-authenticated calls: use the wrapper `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh` — it performs the CSRF + cookie login dance (verified working: login POST → 302, `/users/settings` with session → 200). Examples: `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh /users/settings -i` (default owner creds) or `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test "qa password 1234" /accounts -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}"`. Set `BASE_URL` to override the default `http://127.0.0.1:4100`.

### mix run (seeds and one-off setup)

Use to (re)seed QA data: `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` (idempotent). Run the server itself with `mix phx.server` (background); confirm it's up with `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:4100/` → 200. Reset the dev DB entirely with `mix ecto.reset` (drops, recreates, migrates, runs `priv/repo/seeds.exs`), then re-run the QA seeds. Integration credential checks live in `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/verify_*.sh` (stripe, twilio, resend, object_storage, codemyspec) — each prints one-line JSON with `"status": "ok"|"error"`; they need env vars documented in `.code_my_spec/integrations/index.md`.

## Seed Strategy

Single Repo (`CleanerCrm.Repo`, Postgres, dev DB `cleaner_crm_dev`). One QA seed script:

- `priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` — run with `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Idempotent (checks by email / existing account before inserting). Creates through real context flows (register → magic-link confirm → set password): **owner** `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, **cleaner** `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, and one account **QA Sparkle Cleaning Co** owned by the owner (`Accounts.create_account/2`). Prints credentials and the login URL on completion. Run it after every `mix ecto.reset`, and before any browser session that needs a logged-in user. As domain contexts land (Clients, Scheduling, Quality, …), extend this script with clients/properties/plans rather than adding bash loops — one BEAM boot, all entities.
- `priv/repo/seeds.exs` — stock Phoenix seed file, currently empty; runs automatically during `mix ecto.setup`/`ecto.reset`.

## System Issues

### Port 4000 occupied by another dev app

Another BEAM app on this machine listens on 4000 (and answers `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` with a `dev.codemyspec.com` issuer — it is NOT this app). Cleaner CRM's dev default was moved to **4100** (`config/runtime.exs`, `PORT` env still wins). If a probe of 4000 returns 200s, you are talking to the wrong app. Status: resolved (default port changed).

### `mix test` is rerouted to `mix agent_test`, which skips `ecto.create`

The harness rewrites `mix test`; on a fresh checkout the test DB may not exist and every test fails with `invalid_catalog_name`. Fix: `MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.create && MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.migrate` once. Status: resolved on this machine, will recur on fresh clones.

## Notes

The `:api` pipeline exists but has no routes yet; when API/webhook endpoints land (Stripe webhooks, Twilio status callbacks, reminder confirm links), add curl rows with real headers here. Emails (magic link, invitations) are viewable at `http://127.0.0.1:4100/dev/mailbox` in dev — use it to extract tokens during browser QA. Integration verify scripts are `pending` until the engineer supplies credentials (see `.code_my_spec/integrations/index.md`).

# QA Story Workflow

The `qa_story` agent task is a per-story QA cycle: write a brief, then execute
it against the running app. The project-wide QA plan
(`.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md`) is a prerequisite — produced upstream by
`qa_setup`, not written here.

QA completion is recorded by a DB-backed attempt via `submit_qa_result`. There
is no result.md file in the loop. Findings are filed via `create_issue` as
they're uncovered and linked into the attempt by id.

## Phase 1: Testing brief

**Artifact:** `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md`

The brief is the concrete plan for testing this story — which tools to use,
how to authenticate, what scenarios to test, and what to assert.

Procedure:

1. Read `.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md` for App Overview, Tools Registry,
   auth strategy, and Seed Strategy.
2. Run seed scripts to verify setup works for this story.
3. If this story needs additional seeds or plan updates, make them now
   and update plan.md (don't fork into a story-specific plan).
4. Read the BDD spec files listed in the prompt. They have selectors,
   test data, and assertions.
5. If a linked component is listed in the prompt, read its source and
   spec to understand the feature.
6. Write the brief to `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md` matching
   the `qa_story_brief` document spec from the prompt.

## Phase 2: Execute tests

There is no `result.md` artifact in this phase. Findings flow through
`create_issue` as you discover them; the run ends with one call to
`submit_qa_result`.

### Tool rules — pick by Phoenix pipeline, not by guess

- **UI / LiveView (`:browser` pipeline):** MCP browser tools only.
  Navigate, click, type, screenshot. Log in via the browser (credentials
  and login steps are in the plan).
- **API endpoints (`:api` pipeline):** `curl` with API key headers.
  ALWAYS single-line commands. Use
  `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh` for API-key auth.
- **NEVER** use curl with session cookies or CSRF tokens for
  browser-authenticated routes. If a route is behind
  `:require_authenticated_user`, test it with MCP browser tools.

### Testing approach

- Capture a screenshot at each key state (initial load, after
  interactions, success/error states). Save to
  `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/screenshots/`. Screenshots are evidence
  and remain valuable — attach the path in the issue description for
  any finding that ships a screenshot.
- After scripted scenarios, explore freely: unexpected inputs, edge
  cases, empty states, anything that feels off.
- Reference existing scripts in `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/` by path
  rather than inlining shell commands.

### Filing findings

The moment you observe something wrong — a broken UI, a 500, a missing
feature, an unexpected behavior — call `create_issue` and hold the
returned id. Don't accumulate findings in a notepad. Don't write them
into a markdown file. The DB issue is the canonical record.

- `title` — short, scannable.
- `severity` — critical / high / medium / low / info.
- `scope` — `app` for app-under-development bugs; `qa` for QA infrastructure
  problems; `docs` for docs gaps; (`framework` is a server-side concept and
  not selectable from the local list_issues filter, but `create_issue`
  itself supports it for harness issues).
- `story_id` — the story this finding relates to, when relevant.
- `description` — the reproduction, the expected vs actual, file paths,
  and any screenshot or evidence path.

If a finding is a duplicate of an existing issue (you'll see them in the
prompt's "Existing Issues" section), don't refile.

### Procedure

1. Read the brief at `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md` for the
   complete plan.
2. Read `.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md` for auth strategy and seed commands.
3. Read `priv/knowledge/qa-tooling.md` and `priv/knowledge/qa-tooling/`
   for tool usage patterns.
4. Run seed scripts to set up test data.
5. If a linked component is listed in the prompt, read its source to
   understand implementation details.
6. Execute each test scenario from the brief.
7. Capture screenshots at key states (save to the screenshots directory).
8. For every finding, call `create_issue` immediately and remember the id.
9. If you find a gap in the plan or the brief, fix it in-flight — update
   `plan.md` or `brief.md` rather than working around the gap.
10. Call `submit_qa_result` once at the end with `status`, the structured
    `scenarios` list, and the full `issue_ids` list. Then stop the session.

## What the evaluator does when you stop

The evaluator runs a thin check chain:

1. Validates that `.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md` exists with required sections.
   (If missing, returns invalid pointing at `qa_setup`.)
2. Validates that `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md` exists and parses.
3. Checks whether a DB-backed pass attempt exists via
   `CodeMySpec.Qa.qa_complete?/2`. If yes, the requirement is satisfied
   and the session ends.
4. If no DB attempt exists but the brief is valid, feedback is returned
   demanding a `submit_qa_result` call. The requirement does NOT satisfy
   off a brief alone.

## The submit_qa_result contract

```
submit_qa_result(
  task_id: <task_id from start_task>,
  status: "pass" | "partial" | "fail",
  scenarios: [
    %{name: "...", status: "pass|partial|fail", observation: "..."},
    ...
  ],
  issue_ids: [<every id returned from create_issue this run>]
)
```

Rules:

- `status: "pass"` with `issue_ids: []` is allowed — clean pass, nothing to
  file.
- `status: "partial"` or `"fail"` with `issue_ids: []` is **rejected** by
  the tool. File the findings first.
- Only `status: "pass"` satisfies the `qa_complete` requirement. Other
  statuses record an audit row but leave the requirement open.
- Resubmitting on the same `task_id` is allowed — each call creates a new
  attempt; the latest is canonical.

# QA Tooling Patterns

Guide for writing QA test infrastructure for Phoenix LiveView apps. Covers Vibium MCP browser automation, seed data scripts, and smoke tests.

## Tool selection: Vibium MCP vs curl

**Use the right tool for the right layer.** Getting this wrong wastes time and creates fragile scripts.

| What you're testing | Tool | Auth mechanism | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| UI pages, LiveViews, forms, navigation | **Vibium MCP** | Browser session (login via MCP tools, persist with `browser_storage_state`) | `browser_navigate` + `browser_map` |
| API endpoints (`/api/*`) | **curl** | `X-Api-Key` header, bearer token, or no auth | `curl -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" /api/transactions/1` |
| Webhooks | **curl** | Webhook signature or no auth | `curl -X POST -d '...' /api/webhooks/card-swipe` |
| Smoke tests (route reachability) | **curl** | None (just check HTTP status codes) | `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' /` |

### The golden rule

**Never use curl for session-authenticated routes.** Phoenix session auth requires signed cookies, CSRF tokens, and form POSTs — scraping HTML for tokens is fragile and wrong. If the route is behind `:browser` pipeline + `:require_authenticated_user`, use Vibium MCP.

**Never use Vibium MCP for API endpoints.** API routes don't render HTML — there's nothing to click or screenshot. Use curl with the appropriate header.

### How Phoenix apps split auth

Most Phoenix apps have two pipelines in the router:

- **`:browser`** — session-based auth, CSRF protection, HTML responses. All LiveViews and page controllers live here. **-> Vibium MCP**
- **`:api`** — stateless auth (API keys, bearer tokens, webhook signatures), JSON responses. **-> curl**

Look at the router to determine which pipeline a route uses. That tells you which tool to use.

### `authenticated_curl.sh`

This script wraps curl with the account's API key. It's for API endpoints only — not for session-authenticated pages. If you need to test a LiveView page, use Vibium MCP tools.

## Seed data scripts (.exs)

Seed scripts go in `priv/repo/` and run via `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Each script boots the BEAM once and runs all seed logic in-process.

### Why `.exs`, not bash

A bash script that calls `mix run -e '...'` per entity boots the entire Elixir application from scratch each time — compiling, connecting to the database, starting supervision trees. For 9 entities, that's 9 full boots. A single `.exs` script does it in one.

### Reference script: `priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`

```elixir
# priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs
#
# Creates a complete QA test dataset.
# Idempotent — safe to run multiple times.
#
# Usage: mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs

alias MyApp.{Accounts, Repo}
alias MyApp.Accounts.User

# --- Helper ---
defmodule QaSeed do
  def find_or_create(queryable, unique_field, unique_value, create_fn) do
    import Ecto.Query
    case Repo.one(from r in queryable, where: field(r, ^unique_field) == ^unique_value) do
      nil ->
        {:ok, record} = create_fn.()
        IO.puts("  Created: #{inspect(unique_value)}")
        record
      existing ->
        IO.puts("  Exists: #{inspect(unique_value)}")
        existing
    end
  end
end

# --- 1. User ---
IO.puts("\n--- User ---")
user = case Accounts.get_user_by_email("qa@example.com") do
  nil ->
    {:ok, user} = Accounts.register_user(%{email: "qa@example.com"})
    {:ok, {user, _}} = Accounts.update_user_password(user, %{password: "hello world!"})
    IO.puts("  Created: qa@example.com")
    user
  user ->
    IO.puts("  Exists: qa@example.com")
    user
end

scope = MyApp.Users.Scope.for_user(user)

# --- 2. More entities using context functions ---
IO.puts("\n--- Account ---")
account = QaSeed.find_or_create(MyApp.Accounts.Account, :name, "QA Account", fn ->
  Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "QA Account"})
end)

# ... more entities, each using context functions with scope

# --- Summary ---
IO.puts("""

==========================================
 QA Seed Data — Credentials
==========================================

Email:    qa@example.com
Password: hello world!
URL:      http://localhost:4000/users/log-in
""")
```

### Patterns

- **Idempotency**: check for existing records before inserting. Use context `get_by` functions or Ecto queries.
- **Use context functions**: call `Accounts.create_user(scope, attrs)` not `Repo.insert(%User{...})`. This ensures validations, associations, and side effects run.
- **Build Scope**: after creating the user, build a `Scope` to pass to all subsequent context calls.
- **Print credentials**: always print login info, URLs, and entity IDs at the end.
- **Multiple scripts**: split into separate files for different scenarios (base entities vs. specific test flows). Each is independently runnable.

## Smoke test scripts

For hitting every route and checking for 500s:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

BASE_URL="${APP_URL:-http://localhost:4000}"
FAIL=0

smoke() {
  local path="$1"
  local expected="${2:-200}"

  HTTP_CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$BASE_URL$path")

  if [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "$expected" ]; then
    echo "  PASS GET $path -> $HTTP_CODE"
  else
    echo "  FAIL GET $path -> $HTTP_CODE (expected $expected)"
    FAIL=1
  fi
}

# Public routes
smoke "/"
smoke "/users/log-in"
smoke "/users/register"

```

```
# 4. Fill password

# 5. Click "Log in and stay logged in"
```

```
browser_click(selector: "a[href='/users/log-out']")
```

# QA Tooling Patterns

Guide for writing QA test infrastructure for Phoenix LiveView apps. Covers Vibium MCP browser automation, seed data scripts, and smoke tests.

## Tool selection: Vibium MCP vs curl

**Use the right tool for the right layer.** Getting this wrong wastes time and creates fragile scripts.

| What you're testing | Tool | Auth mechanism | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| UI pages, LiveViews, forms, navigation | **Vibium MCP** | Browser session (login via MCP tools, persist with `browser_storage_state`) | `browser_navigate` + `browser_map` |
| API endpoints (`/api/*`) | **curl** | `X-Api-Key` header, bearer token, or no auth | `curl -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" /api/transactions/1` |
| Webhooks | **curl** | Webhook signature or no auth | `curl -X POST -d '...' /api/webhooks/card-swipe` |
| Smoke tests (route reachability) | **curl** | None (just check HTTP status codes) | `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' /` |

### The golden rule

**Never use curl for session-authenticated routes.** Phoenix session auth requires signed cookies, CSRF tokens, and form POSTs — scraping HTML for tokens is fragile and wrong. If the route is behind `:browser` pipeline + `:require_authenticated_user`, use Vibium MCP.

**Never use Vibium MCP for API endpoints.** API routes don't render HTML — there's nothing to click or screenshot. Use curl with the appropriate header.

### How Phoenix apps split auth

Most Phoenix apps have two pipelines in the router:

- **`:browser`** — session-based auth, CSRF protection, HTML responses. All LiveViews and page controllers live here. **-> Vibium MCP**
- **`:api`** — stateless auth (API keys, bearer tokens, webhook signatures), JSON responses. **-> curl**

Look at the router to determine which pipeline a route uses. That tells you which tool to use.

### `authenticated_curl.sh`

This script wraps curl with the account's API key. It's for API endpoints only — not for session-authenticated pages. If you need to test a LiveView page, use Vibium MCP tools.

## Seed data scripts (.exs)

Seed scripts go in `priv/repo/` and run via `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Each script boots the BEAM once and runs all seed logic in-process.

### Why `.exs`, not bash

A bash script that calls `mix run -e '...'` per entity boots the entire Elixir application from scratch each time — compiling, connecting to the database, starting supervision trees. For 9 entities, that's 9 full boots. A single `.exs` script does it in one.

### Reference script: `priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`

```elixir
# priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs
#
# Creates a complete QA test dataset.
# Idempotent — safe to run multiple times.
#
# Usage: mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs

alias MyApp.{Accounts, Repo}
alias MyApp.Accounts.User

# --- Helper ---
defmodule QaSeed do
  def find_or_create(queryable, unique_field, unique_value, create_fn) do
    import Ecto.Query
    case Repo.one(from r in queryable, where: field(r, ^unique_field) == ^unique_value) do
      nil ->
        {:ok, record} = create_fn.()
        IO.puts("  Created: #{inspect(unique_value)}")
        record
      existing ->
        IO.puts("  Exists: #{inspect(unique_value)}")
        existing
    end
  end
end

# --- 1. User ---
IO.puts("\n--- User ---")
user = case Accounts.get_user_by_email("qa@example.com") do
  nil ->
    {:ok, user} = Accounts.register_user(%{email: "qa@example.com"})
    {:ok, {user, _}} = Accounts.update_user_password(user, %{password: "hello world!"})
    IO.puts("  Created: qa@example.com")
    user
  user ->
    IO.puts("  Exists: qa@example.com")
    user
end

scope = MyApp.Users.Scope.for_user(user)

# --- 2. More entities using context functions ---
IO.puts("\n--- Account ---")
account = QaSeed.find_or_create(MyApp.Accounts.Account, :name, "QA Account", fn ->
  Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "QA Account"})
end)

# ... more entities, each using context functions with scope

# --- Summary ---
IO.puts("""

==========================================
 QA Seed Data — Credentials
==========================================

Email:    qa@example.com
Password: hello world!
URL:      http://localhost:4000/users/log-in
""")
```

### Patterns

- **Idempotency**: check for existing records before inserting. Use context `get_by` functions or Ecto queries.
- **Use context functions**: call `Accounts.create_user(scope, attrs)` not `Repo.insert(%User{...})`. This ensures validations, associations, and side effects run.
- **Build Scope**: after creating the user, build a `Scope` to pass to all subsequent context calls.
- **Print credentials**: always print login info, URLs, and entity IDs at the end.
- **Multiple scripts**: split into separate files for different scenarios (base entities vs. specific test flows). Each is independently runnable.

## Smoke test scripts

For hitting every route and checking for 500s:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

BASE_URL="${APP_URL:-http://localhost:4000}"
FAIL=0

smoke() {
  local path="$1"
  local expected="${2:-200}"

  HTTP_CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$BASE_URL$path")

  if [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "$expected" ]; then
    echo "  PASS GET $path -> $HTTP_CODE"
  else
    echo "  FAIL GET $path -> $HTTP_CODE (expected $expected)"
    FAIL=1
  fi
}

smoke "/users/log-in"
smoke "/users/register"

# Authenticated routes should redirect to login
smoke "/accounts" 302

exit $FAIL
```

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story832.Criterion7107Spex do
  @moduledoc """

  Criterion 7107 — Adding a property under an existing client saves it
  and lists it under that client as its only owning client.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "owner adds a property to an existing client" do
    scenario "the property is saved and listed under its client" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client \"Sarah Kim\" exists", context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Sarah Kim")
        {:ok, Map.put(context, :client_path, client_path)}
      end

      when_ "the owner adds a property \"123 Oak St\" and assigns it to Sarah Kim", context do
        property_path =
          create_property(context.conn, context.client_path, %{service_address: "123 Oak St"})

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :property_path, property_path)}
      end

      then_ "the property is saved and listed under Sarah Kim", context do

        assert html =~ "123 Oak St"

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story832.Criterion7118Spex do

  Criterion 7118 — A client with upcoming scheduled jobs cannot be
  permanently deleted; the owner is directed to deactivate instead.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "owner attempts to hard-delete a client with upcoming jobs" do
    scenario "the hard delete is blocked" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client with a job scheduled next week", context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Taylor Brooks")

        property_path =
          create_property(context.conn, client_path, %{service_address: "3 Willow Way"})

        schedule_job(context.conn, property_path, next_week())

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :client_path, client_path)}
      end

      when_ "the owner attempts to permanently delete the client", context do
        {:ok, show_live, _html} = live(context.conn, context.client_path)

        html =
          show_live
          |> element("[data-test='delete-client-button']")
          |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :delete_result_html, html)}
      end

      then_ "the deletion is blocked", context do
        {:ok, _index_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/clients")
        assert html =~ "Taylor Brooks"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the owner is told to deactivate the client or first remove its upcoming jobs",
            context do
        assert context.delete_result_html =~ "deactivate"
        assert context.delete_result_html =~ "upcoming job"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp create_client(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =

    path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    schedule_live
    |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
      job: %{property_id: property_id, scheduled_date: scheduled_date}
    )
    |> render_submit()

    :ok
  end

  defp next_week do
    Date.utc_today() |> Date.add(7) |> Date.to_iso8601()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent do @moduledoc """ Create a single job, or assign/reassign a cleaner to an existing one. ## Assigns | Assign | Type | Required | Description | |---------------|-----------------|----------|-------------------------------------------------------| | id | string | yes | LiveComponent DOM id | | current_scope | `Scope.t()` | yes | caller scope, used for all context calls | | action | `:new \\| :assign` | yes | `:new` renders the full job form; `:assign` renders just the cleaner picker for an existing job | | job | `Job.t()` | yes | blank `%Job{}` for `:new`, loaded job for `:assign` | On a successful `:new` save, navigates itself to the new job's show page. On a successful `:assign`, sends `{__MODULE__, {:saved, job}}` to the parent instead (there's nowhere further to go — the parent just refreshes). Two more actions embed this same component inline on `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Index` (the board) rather than standalone: `:quick_new` (the board's own "New Job" button — same form as `:new`, but sends `{__MODULE__, {:job_created, job}}` to the parent instead of navigating away, since the point is to see the new job's brief on the board itself) and `:edit` (the board's per-job "Edit" button — reschedule and/or price change via `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.update_job/3`, sending `{__MODULE__, {:job_updated, job}}`). Neither touches `cleaner_id` — (re)assignment stays on the conflict-checked `:assign` path. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component import Ecto.Query, warn: false alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property alias CleanerCrm.Repo alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job @impl true def render(%{action: :assign} = assigns) do ~H"""
<.header>Assign Cleaner

{@conflict_error}

<.form for={@form} id={"#{@id}-form"} data-test="assignment-form" phx-target={@myself} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save" > <.input field={@form[:cleaner_id]} type="select" label="Cleaner" prompt="Unassigned" options={cleaner_options(@cleaners)} />
<.button phx-disable-with="Assigning...">Assign Cleaner
""" end def render(%{action: :edit} = assigns) do ~H""" === client form_component === defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.FormComponent do @moduledoc """ Create/edit a client's name and billing preference. On successful save, navigates to the client's own page directly (rather than notifying the parent to do it) — a parent's `handle_info` reacting to a component's self-sent message runs one mailbox message after the "save" event's own reply, too late for `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.render_submit/1` to observe the redirect. ## Assigns | Assign | Type | Required | Description | |---------------|---------------|----------|----------------------------------------| | id | string | yes | LiveComponent DOM id | | current_scope | `Scope.t()` | yes | caller scope, used for all context calls | | action | `:new \\| :edit` | yes | which mode the form is in | | client | `Client.t()` | yes | `%Client{}` (blank for `:new`, loaded for `:edit`) | ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Clients` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_component alias CleanerCrm.Clients @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H"""
<.header>{form_title(@action)} <.form for={@form} id={"#{@id}-form"} data-test="client-form" phx-target={@myself} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save" > <.input field={@form[:name]} type="text" label="Name" /> <.input field={@form[:card_on_file]} type="checkbox" label="Card on file" />
<.button phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save Client
""" end @impl true def update(%{client: client} = assigns, socket) do changeset = Clients.change_client(assigns.current_scope, client) {:ok, socket |> assign(assigns) |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset))} end @impl true def handle_event("validate", %{"client" => client_params}, socket) do changeset = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Clients.change_client(socket.assigns.client, client_params) |> Map.put(:action, :validate) {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end def handle_event("save", %{"client" => client_params}, socket) do save_client(socket, socket.assigns.action, client_params) end defp save_client(socket, :new, params) do case Clients.create_client(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do {:ok, client} -> {:noreply, push_navigate(socket, to: ~p"/clients/#{client}")} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end end defp save_client(socket, :edit, params) do case Clients.update_client(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.client, params) do {:ok, client} -> {:noreply, push_navigate(socket, to: ~p"/clients/#{client}")} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset))} end end defp form_title(:new), do: "New Client" defp form_title(:edit), do: "Edit Client" end

# Qa Story Brief

Story 832 — Manage clients and properties with access details

## Tool

web

## Auth

Log in as the owner via the browser (this story's surfaces — `/clients`,
`/properties/*`, `/schedule` — are all under `:require_authenticated_user`,
so use Vibium MCP browser tools, never curl with cookies).

1. `browser_launch(headless: true)`
2. `browser_navigate(url: "http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in")`
3. `browser_scroll_into_view(selector: "#login_form_password")`
4. `browser_fill(selector: "input[name=\"user[email]\"]", value: "qa-owner@cleanercrm.test")`
5. `browser_fill(selector: "input[name=\"user[password]\"]", value: "qa password 1234")`
6. Click the password form's submit button ("Log in" inside `#login_form_password`)
7. `browser_wait_for_url(pattern: "/")` — success redirects to `/`

Cleaner login (only needed if a cleaner-vs-owner permission check comes up):
`qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, same form.

## Seeds

```
mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs
```

Idempotent. Creates owner `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test`, cleaner
`qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` (both password `qa password 1234`), and account
"QA Sparkle Cleaning Co". No clients/properties/jobs are pre-seeded by this
script — create them live during the test scenarios below using the app's
own forms (each scenario is self-contained and creates its own client).

## What To Test

Routes (confirmed in `lib/cleaner_crm_web/router.ex`): `/clients`,
`/clients/new`, `/clients/:id`, `/clients/:id/edit`,
`/clients/:id/properties/new`, `/properties/new`, `/properties/:id`,
`/properties/:id/edit`, `/schedule`.

- **Add a property under an existing client** (criterion 7107): create
  client "Sarah Kim" via `/clients/new` (`[data-test='client-form']`,
  field `client[name]`) → submit → redirects to `/clients/:id`. From
  there click "Add Property" → `/clients/:id/properties/new`. Fill
  `[data-test='property-form']` field `property[service_address]` =
  "123 Oak St" → submit. Expect redirect to `/properties/:id`. Verify the
  client's show page (`/clients/:id`) lists "123 Oak St". Verify the
  property page shows `[data-test='property-client']` containing "Sarah
  Kim" exactly once (no client picker shown, since client was
  preselected from this route).

- **Reject a property with no client** (criterion 7108): navigate
  directly to `/properties/new` (no client preselected — a client
  `<select>` should render). Fill only
  `property[service_address]` = "123 Oak St", leave the client select
  unset, submit. Expect the form stays on the page (no navigation) and
  `[data-test='client-error']` shows text containing "is required".

- **Save a property with a valid service address** (criterion 7109):
  create client "Priya Nair", go to its "add property" form, fill
  `property[service_address]` = "123 Oak St, Austin, TX", submit.
  Expect redirect to `/properties/:id` and the page shows "123 Oak St,
  Austin, TX".

- **Reject a property with a blank address** (criterion 7110): on the
  same "add property" form (client preselected), leave
  `property[service_address]` blank, submit. Expect the form stays put
  and `[data-test='service-address-error']` shows text containing "is
  required".

- **Job brief inherits property access details** (criterion 7111):
  create client "Devon Ashe", add a property "77 Maple Ave" with
  `property[lockbox_code]` = "4821", `property[parking_notes]` =
  "driveway only", `property[pet_notes]` = "dog in yard" (also fill
  `property[entry_method]` if you want extra coverage — not required by
  the criterion). Go to `/schedule`, click
  `[data-test='new-job-button']`, fill the job form (`job[property_id]`
  = the 77 Maple Ave property via its select option, and the date field
  named `job[date]` — use a date 7+ days out, e.g. today + 7 days in
  `YYYY-MM-DD`), submit. Expect the schedule board / job card to show
  "77 Maple Ave", "4821", "driveway only", and "dog in yard" (the job
  brief).

- **Updated code propagates to future jobs** (criterion 7113): create
  client "Jordan Lee", property "45 Elm St" with `lockbox_code` =
  "4821", schedule a job on it dated 7+ days out (same flow as above).
  Then go to `/properties/:id/edit` for that property, change
  `property[lockbox_code]` to "9077", submit (redirects back to the
  property page). Return to `/schedule` and confirm the job card for
  "45 Elm St" now shows "9077" and does **not** show "4821" anywhere.

- **Entry code change is logged** (criterion 7115): create client "Alex
  Rivera", property "12 Cedar Ct" with `property[alarm_code]` = "1234".
  Edit the property (`/properties/:id/edit`), change
  `property[alarm_code]` to "5678", submit. On the property's show page,
  confirm a heading/section "Access Change History" appears, with a
  `[data-test='audit-entry']` row containing the owner's email
  (`qa-owner@cleanercrm.test`) and the text "alarm code", and that the
  entry element carries a `data-timestamp` attribute (inspect via
  `browser_get_attribute` or `browser_get_html`).

- **Deactivate a client with upcoming jobs** (criterion 7117): create
  client "Morgan Reyes", property "9 Birch Ln", schedule a job 7+ days
  out. On `/clients/:id` click `[data-test='deactivate-client-button']`
  (confirm the native `data-confirm` dialog via
  `browser_dialog_accept` if one appears). Expect the client's header
  now shows "Inactive". Go to `/clients` and confirm "Morgan Reyes" does
  **not** appear in the active list. Return to `/clients/:id` directly
  and confirm the client's name "Morgan Reyes" and its property "9 Birch
  Ln" are still shown (history/properties retained despite being
  hidden from the active index).

- **Block hard delete of a client with upcoming jobs** (criterion
  7118): create client "Taylor Brooks", property "3 Willow Way",
  schedule a job 7+ days out. On `/clients/:id` click
  `[data-test='delete-client-button']` (accept the confirm dialog).
  Expect deletion is blocked: a flash/error message mentioning
  "deactivate" and "upcoming job(s)" appears, and the client still
  exists — check `/clients` (if still active) or `/clients/:id` shows
  "Taylor Brooks" still present, not deleted.

- **Exploratory (not a numbered criterion but worth a quick check):**
  the client form (`[data-test='client-form']`) also has a
  `client[card_on_file]` checkbox — confirm it doesn't block a plain
  name-only submit. On `/clients/new`, submitting a blank name should
  presumably error too — try it and note actual behavior even though
  it's not an explicit acceptance criterion.

## Result Path

No result.md file — file findings via `create_issue` as discovered and
call `mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__submit_qa_result` with
`task_id: e4939525-62c6-4611-9e1f-04207dea11ba` at the end. Save
screenshots to `.code_my_spec/qa/832/screenshots/`.

## Setup Notes

- All property/client/schedule pages are LiveViews under
  `CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.Show` (`/clients/:id`, `/properties/:id`,
  edit variants) and `CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.Index` (`/clients`),
  `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Index` (`/schedule`) — confirmed by
  reading `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/client_live/show.ex`,
  `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/client_live/property_form_component.ex`, and
  `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/schedule_live/job_form_component.ex`. Use
  those files if a selector below doesn't match what's rendered.
- The property form's client `<select>` only renders when no client is
  preselected (`/properties/new`); from a client's own page
  (`/clients/:id/properties/new`) the client is fixed and hidden.
- The job form's date input is a real `<input type="date">` bound to
  `job[date]` (not `job[scheduled_date]`, which is a hidden decoy field
  in the markup) — fill the visible date input by its label "Date" or
  by id, not by name, to avoid the hidden field.
- Each scenario above creates its own client — this avoids cross-test
  interference and mirrors the BDD spex fixtures at
  `test/spex/832_manage_clients_and_properties_with_access_details/`.

input.title: Vibium browser session appears shared/contended across concurrent QA agents, making browser-based testing unreliable
input.description:
While running the per-story QA session for story 832 (Manage clients and properties with access details), the Vibium browser instance would not stay on any page I navigated to. Reproduction: called browser_navigate(url: "http://127.0.0.1:4100/clients"), tool returned "Navigated to http://127.0.0.1:4100/clients", then immediately calling browser_evaluate("window.location.href") returned "http://127.0.0.1:4100/schedule" instead. This happened repeatedly and deterministically across multiple attempts (including on brand-new pages/tabs opened via browser_new_page, which also got redirected to /schedule or /schedule/plans/new moments after creation, before any action of mine). browser_list_pages showed 3 open tabs all pointing at /schedule-family URLs (/schedule, /schedule/plans/new) that I never navigated to.

This strongly suggests the local Vibium browser automation server is a single shared Chrome instance across concurrent agent sessions (not isolated per QA task), and another concurrent session (likely QA for a Scheduling-related story) was actively driving navigation on the same browser, overwriting my pages within milliseconds of my own calls. I could not find any browser_start parameter for session/profile isolation, and browser_new_page/browser_switch_page did not provide effective isolation from the interference.

Impact: browser-based QA (the required tool per the QA plan's tool-selection rule for LiveView/session-authenticated routes) is currently unreliable for any concurrently-running QA session on this machine. I was unable to complete UI-driven scenario testing for story 832 as a result.

Expected: each QA agent session gets an isolated browser context/profile (or the tooling serializes/queues concurrent browser automation sessions) so navigation and DOM state observed by one agent aren't clobbered by another agent's concurrent actions.

input.title: Client show page uses native data-confirm instead of project's confirm_dialog pattern
input.description:
The Deactivate and Delete buttons on the client show page (lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/client_live/show.ex) use the built-in `data-confirm` attribute, which triggers a native browser confirm() dialog:

  <.button phx-click="deactivate-client" data-test="deactivate-client-button" data-confirm="Deactivate this client?" ...>
  <.button phx-click="delete-client" data-test="delete-client-button" data-confirm="Permanently delete this client?" ...>

Project convention (per team memory/lesson) is to avoid `data-confirm` because native dialogs are effectively untestable via browser automation, and to use the project's own `confirm_dialog` CoreComponents pattern instead (an in-DOM dialog/modal that a test can find and click).

Impact observed during QA (story 832, criteria 7117/7118): driving these two buttons via Vibium browser automation was unreliable — clicks silently no-op'd, required overriding window.confirm from JS to get a response, and page state occasionally desynced from the intended client after clicking (once causing an unintended deactivate/reactivate on the wrong client, which I had to manually undo). A `confirm_dialog`-based modal would have exposed clickable in-DOM confirm/cancel buttons instead, making the flow both more testable and more consistent with the rest of the app's UI patterns.

Suggested fix: replace both `data-confirm` attributes with the project's `confirm_dialog` CoreComponents component/pattern.

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.Scope do
  @moduledoc """
  Defines the scope of the caller to be used throughout the app.

  The `CleanerCrm.Users.Scope` allows public interfaces to receive
  information about the caller, such as if the call is initiated from an
  end-user, and if so, which user. Additionally, such a scope can carry fields
  such as "super user" or other privileges for use in authorization checks,
  or to ensure specific code paths can only be accessed for a given scope.

  It is useful for logging as well as for scoping pubsub subscriptions and
  broadcasts when a caller subscribes to an interface or performs a particular
  action.

  Feel free to extend the fields on this struct to fit the needs of
  growing application requirements.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  defstruct user: nil,
            active_account: nil,
            active_account_id: nil

  @doc """
  Creates a scope for the given user.

  Returns nil if no user is given.
  """
  def for_user(%User{} = user) do
    %__MODULE__{user: user}
  end

  def for_user(nil), do: nil
end

## Client show page uses native data-confirm instead of project's confirm_dialog pattern (ID: b1bf9695-3548-4138-bcff-9b31e873e790)

**Severity:** medium | **Scope:** app | **Status:** resolved | **Story:** 832

The Deactivate and Delete buttons on the client show page (lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/client_live/show.ex) use the built-in `data-confirm` attribute, which triggers a native browser confirm() dialog:

  <.button phx-click="deactivate-client" data-test="deactivate-client-button" data-confirm="Deactivate this client?" ...>
  <.button phx-click="delete-client" data-test="delete-client-button" data-confirm="Permanently delete this client?" ...>

Project convention (per team memory/lesson) is to avoid `data-confirm` because native dialogs are effectively untestable via browser automation, and to use the project's own `confirm_dialog` CoreComponents pattern instead (an in-DOM dialog/modal that a test can find and click).

Impact observed during QA (story 832, criteria 7117/7118): driving these two buttons via Vibium browser automation was unreliable — clicks silently no-op'd, required overriding window.confirm from JS to get a response, and page state occasionally desynced from the intended client after clicking (once causing an unintended deactivate/reactivate on the wrong client, which I had to manually undo). A `confirm_dialog`-based modal would have exposed clickable in-DOM confirm/cancel buttons instead, making the flow both more testable and more consistent with the rest of the app's UI patterns.

Suggested fix: replace both `data-confirm` attributes with the project's `confirm_dialog` CoreComponents component/pattern.

**Resolution:** Fixed app-wide during this QA session: all six data-confirm usages (client show deactivate/delete, account delete, member remove, invitation cancel, integration disconnect) were replaced with the confirm_dialog CoreComponents pattern (ported from code_my_spec) — DaisyUI dialog, show_confirm/1 trigger, stable [data-role='confirm-confirm']/[data-role='confirm-cancel'] selectors. Zero data-confirm attributes remain in lib/ (only a docstring mention). Two affected BDD specs (832 criteria 7117/7118) updated to drive the dialog; full suite 100/100 green, mix test 146/146. The QA agent's observation predated the fix landing (its page was mounted before the code reloaded).
